answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in an on-chain bond before it may trade or claim rewards. The bond stays at risk: if an identity is caught duplicating another agent’s signed work or breaking an agreed rule, anyone can submit the evidence and trigger a slashing vote. A sybil swarm must therefore tie up capital for every persona, while detection can destroy those deposits; it cannot cheaply wander from haven to haven or dominate a ridge of accounts at no cost.
